Prevention: Apply organic manure/ fertilizer to promote good plant health and vigour
Promote good soil and water conservation practices
Regularly monitor for the presence of twig borer symptoms on alternative host such as avocado, cocoa within proximity of a coffee field
Monitoring: Use ethanol baited traps (pour the ethanol in empty water bottles and create two holes on each side) to monitor populations and outbreak
Check daily for the presence of wilting, yellowing, dry/ dead small branches/twigs with small holes (bicycle spoke size) at the entry point especially during the dry season.
Split the affected branches to check for presence of a white spongy (fungal) growth and small light brown to shiny black beetles
Look out for light green leaves of infested branches on coffee plants
Direct Control: Prune and burn all infested branches/twigs, but this is time consuming
Provide additional water if availabl during dry period
Encourage other farmers within the area to control the twig borer
This will help with resistance to infestation or recovering from attack
Restrictions: Consult your extension worker and always read the label for direction on use
Always wear protective gear (overalls, gumboots, goggles, caps, gloves and face masks) when handling chemicals
